name: Pro5 TLR

origin.basis: French tire maker; Michelin's UK site lists its bicycle range and dealers.

manufacturing.basis: Michelin's size list does not state where these tires are made.

positioning: Endurance tubeless tire focused on air tightness, easier mounting and longevity.
hookless_note: Michelin lists every size (28-40 mm) for hooked and hookless rims.
weight_basis: Maker claims as listed by Bicycle Rolling Resistance for 28 and 32 mm; Michelin's size list shows no weights.
pressure_note: Michelin's size list gives no maximum pressure; use the figure printed on the tire.

availability.note: Sold by Michelin's official Tmall store in mainland China; listed on Michelin's UK site with a dealer locator; North American availability not verified in this pass.

price_observations.market: Michelin official Tmall store (米其林官方旗舰店)
price_observations.conditions: Tmall list price before discounts ('优惠前') on 2026-11-01; the listing text does not say whether the option is one tire or a pair. Shipping within mainland China. A store coupon showed CNY 467.08.

caveats: The 32 mm lab sample measured 31 mm, outside the comparable rolling-resistance bands.
Weights for 30, 35 and 40 mm were not found.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-03 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list in a browser (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Corrected on 2026-11-03: the first check of Bicycle Rolling Resistance's index missed this tire's test pages; their reader comments are now read. Comments on a TLR test page count for this tire unless the owner names another version; a report of no grip on wet singletrack is not coded as wet road grip.

reports.summary: Easy to mount, pleasant and fun to ride (transparent-sidewall colour option).
Very pleased with the 32 mm so far: it rides as well as the GP5000 TR it replaced, though it was very tight to fit.
Likes how the 30 mm rides and finds it good value at sale prices; its one puncture so far sealed eventually.
Loves the 32 and 35 mm on winter wheels: very good handling and grip, not slow, an all-rounder between the GP5000 S TR and the GP5000 All Season.
A good tire that gives confidence and is stable on descents, but it feels noticeably slower than the 28 mm GP5000 on the owner's other wheelset.
About a year of road riding: very good grip and durability and tread wear that looks good so far, perhaps a little slower than the GP5000s it replaced.
Nothing but excellent over a couple of months of commuting, group rides and rough bikepacking trails: fast, cheaper than most and easy to set up tubeless.
Great on the road and on dry terrain over a few thousand km, though it has no grip on wet singletrack.
After one ride, impressed by how quick and comfortable it was off road; on wide rims it measured too wide for the owner's frame.
First rides put it near the top of the 35 mm tires the owner has used: smooth, fast-feeling, consistent and confident in corners, with the easiest setup and best air retention.
Fun, fast and stable; corners well and handles a little gravel without damage.
Very fast and smooth on the road and comfortable on light gravel; a major improvement on the 35 mm GravelKing slicks it replaced.
Very pleased after about 500 km on an all-road bike: fast, stable and absorbs bumps very well.
Good value and suited to autumn riding; rolls acceptably and wears little.
Pretty good on a first ride, though the owner was not yet confident cornering on it.
